concerns.text: T009c (Document power analysis results) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly lists 'Dependency: T009b must complete first'. A task cannot be parallel-safe if it has a hard ordering dependency on another task in the same phase. T009c must be sequential to T009b.

T010 and T011 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but their descriptions state 'MUST run after T013 completes' and 'MUST run after T014 completes' respectively. Since T013 and T014 are the producers of the artifacts these tests consume, T010/T011 cannot run in parallel with T013/T014. The [P] tag is semantically incorrect for the execution window relative to their producers.

T016 (Cleaning) and T017 (Randomization Validation) are marked [P] and listed as runnable in parallel. However, T016 requires the 'full set of stimuli' (from T013) and 'rated stimuli count' (from T014) to perform listwise deletion. T017 also requires T014 output. While they can run in parallel *with each other*, the description 'can run independently of generation logic' is misleading; they are strictly consumers of T013/T014 artifacts. The [P] tag is acceptable only if interpreted as 'parallel to each other', but the text implies independence from producers which is false.

T014b is described as 'Implement validation logic... to enforce minimum N constraint'. The description says 'Dependency: T014'. If T014 generates the data, T014b must run *after* T014. If T014b is a separate script, it cannot be [P] relative to T014. The current phrasing suggests T014b might be a sub-task of T014, but it is listed as a separate task ID. Clarify if T014b is a post-processing step that must strictly follow T014.

T028 (Sensitivity engine) depends on T027 (Definitions) and T025 (Primary results). T029 (Re-execution) depends on T028. The [P] tag is not present on T028/T029, which is correct. However, T027 is not marked [P] but could be (it generates definitions, doesn't consume). This is a minor optimization, not a violation, but the dependency chain T027 -> T028 -> T029 is correctly ordered.
